sections.title: Architecture & Mechanism (Zero-UAC)
sections.content:
The Local Packages module solves a common developer bottleneck: how to efficiently share modular in-house libraries across multiple projects without duplicating code or publishing to private indexes.

VenvHub Pro requires zero administrator elevation (UAC) and creates no fragile NTFS filesystem junctions. Instead, it utilizes high-performance Python Import Hooks (sys.meta_path). The system automatically orchestrates:

  • A ledger file venvhub.json inside the target environment's site-packages.
  • A runtime bootstrap hook (.pth and .py bootstrapper) intercepting imports and mapping them directly to your live repository.
  • Automated background installation of upstream PyPI package requirements.
  • Direct injection of absolute extraPaths and workspace Tasks into VS Code.

sections.title: Package Structure (local_meta.json)
sections.content:
Every shared module directory requires a local_meta.json descriptor defining its identity, version, and dependencies.

Metadata Specification:

{
    "name": "MyDatabase",
    "version": "1.2.0",
    "short_description": "Handles MongoDB persistence and caching",
    "requires_local": ["MyLogger"],
    "requires_pip": ["colorama", "pymongo"],
    "vscode_integration": {
        "tasks": [
            {
                "label": "Flush DB Cache",
                "type": "shell",
                "command": "python -c \"import db; db.clear()\""
            }
        ],
        "keybindings": [
            {
                "key": "ctrl+shift+d",
                "command": "workbench.action.tasks.runTask",
                "args": "Flush DB Cache"
            }
        ]
    }
}
Descriptor KeyFunction
short_descriptionOverview summary displayed inside the VenvHub linker table.
requires_localList of co-dependent module folder names inside the local package root.
requires_pipList of third-party PyPI dependencies to automatically install.
vscode_integrationDefines custom Tasks and Keybindings to dynamically provision to target projects.

sections.title: Configuring Root Storage Path
sections.content:
Configure your shared module repository location:

  1. Open Manager (🖥️) -> Settings tab.
  2. Under Root Paths, locate Local Packages.
  3. Click the folder icon 📁 and choose your repository root directory (where each package lives in its own subfolder).
Portable Drive Binding: On USB flash drives, this path automatically binds relative to the current drive letter.

sections.title: Linking into Virtual Environments
sections.content:
Attaching libraries to target environments:

  1. Right-click target Venv in the Manager matrix.
  2. Select 🔗 Local Packages.
  3. Check the packages you wish to link.
  4. Click 💾 Save Changes (Relink).
Automated Dependency Resolution: Linking 'Package A' which requires 'Package B' parses metadata recursively, maps all search paths into venvhub.json, and installs missing Pip dependencies silently.

sections.title: VS Code Integration (Hybrid Tracker)
sections.content:
One of the primary advantages of VenvHub Pro is seamless, coordinated synchronization with Visual Studio Code:

  • VenvHub Pro inspects venvhub.json and injects absolute paths into python.analysis.extraPaths in your workspace settings.json. IntelliSense instantly resolves your imports.
  • Custom tasks (tasks.json) and keybindings (keybindings.json) are dynamically provisioned based on the package metadata.
🛡️ Hybrid Mechanism (Brutal Check) & venvhub_tracker.json:

To ensure that removing packages never damages your own custom VS Code tasks, the system utilizes a safety tracker:

  1. Receipt Ledger: All injected changes are recorded in .vscode/venvhub_tracker.json.
  2. Safety Brake: If a package directory is deleted manually via Windows Explorer, VenvHub Pro traces orphaned entries and cleanly purges them from VS Code.
  3. Automatic Cleanup: If no tasks remain after unlinking, it physically deletes empty tasks.json and keybindings.json files to keep the workspace clean.

sections.title: Bundling with PyInstaller (.EXE)
sections.content:
Due to the zero-UAC architecture (Import Hooks), local packages are not physically copied into the environment's directory. Standard PyInstaller static analysis would not find them automatically.

VenvHub Auto-Injector (Full Automation):
When creating a standalone .exe, you don't need to do anything extra in the PyInstaller Builder!

Before compilation, VenvHub Pro Builder automatically inspects venvhub.json and generates in the background:
  • The --paths parameter, allowing PyInstaller to immediately discover all Python code from linked local packages.
  • The --add-data parameter for each linked package, automatically embedding images, JSON configurations, and UI templates directly into the final .exe.

sections.title: Self-Healing Paths on USB Drives (Portable Mode)
sections.content:
The hook architecture makes running projects from USB flash drives exceptionally reliable.

Lightning-Fast Silent Auto-Repair: Whenever you launch the application on a new PC:
  1. VenvHub Pro detects the change in drive letter (e.g. from E:\ to F:\).
  2. It opens venvhub.json inside the environment directory.
  3. Instantly and completely silently rewrites outdated drive letters to the new ones in milliseconds without triggering any UAC prompts.

sections.title: Network Drives (NAS & Shared Folders)
sections.content:
✅ Full Support Anywhere!

The root folder of local packages can reside literally anywhere – on a local drive, network-attached storage (NAS), or cloud sync folder. Because VenvHub Pro writes paths purely as standard strings into JSON files, the underlying physical storage type does not matter to the OS.
